newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran recalls ambassador from Germany over verdict.
newsitem.headline: Iran recalls ambassador from Germany over verdict.

text.p: Iran on Thursday withdrew its ambassador from Germany in response to the ruling by a German court that Tehran ordered the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents, Iranian state television said.

"A spokesman for the foreign ministry in a response to the court's political move announced: 'we have recalled our ambassador for certain consultations,'" said the television, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.

A Berlin court in its Thursday ruling avoided citing names but gave the positions of the Iranian officials it believed were behind the murders as members of a committee which included the state president and Iran's religious leader.
Iran's ties with Germany, Tehran's main trade partner, were strained by German charges that spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani ordered the murders.
Iran denies all responsibility for the killings which it blamed on infighting among opposition groups.
There was no immediate reaction from Iran to the ruling and residents in the Iranian capital said they did not see any extra security measures at the German embassy in central Tehran.
But the speaker of the Iranian parliament, Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, dismissed as "political" the court ruling, saying it was untrue and demanding evidence. Nateq-Nouri spoke while on a visit to Moscow.
Iran's state news agency IRNA reported the verdicts against the defendants, but made no mention of the ruling on who ordered the murders.
